prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1367; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed first notice of loss for a left-turn collision at an intersection. Insured reports a vehicle traveling straight through on the opposing approach struck the insured's vehicle during the turn. Police report requested. No citations noted at scene per initial call.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant states they are not represented by an attorney and wishes to handle the claim directly. Claimant reports neck and back strain following the impact and has begun outpatient treatment. Advised claimant of the medical documentation needed for injury evaluation.

Entry 3: Obtained the recorded statement from the insured. Insured states the left-turn signal had turned yellow and the insured proceeded when the opposing lane appeared clear. Photos of both vehicles and the intersection received and added to the file. Liability currently under review.

Entry 4: Received the police report. It notes the opposing driver was cited for failure to yield during a permissive left-turn situation. Witness contact information listed. Scene diagram reviewed and consistent with the insured's account of the impact point. Preliminary liability assessment leans toward the claimant's vehicle as the at-fault party, pending final review.

Entry 5: Followed up with claimant regarding treatment progress. Claimant reports ongoing neck stiffness and lower back discomfort, with a physician's note on file describing a soft tissue strain. Medical records requested with signed authorization. Reserve reviewed and file flagged for supervisor review due to injury component.
